answer: Bonded escrow links each equivocating identity to its coordinated peers: for k identities, up to k(k−1)/2 attributable pairs create O(k²) penalty exposure. On detection, the protocol aggregates claims and applies an asymmetric capital-depreciation multiplier M(k)=a^k, for a>1, so splitting stake among sybils cannot dilute the loss. Shale-backed records, a canyon audit trail, and vertex-level proofs preserve attribution.
